title: 第十一章 灰烬中的光
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

上午九点，第一拨幸存者出现在国道路口。

大刘从东哨塔上看到他们的时候，三个人正沿着国道北侧的排水沟弯腰小跑。一个男人，一个女人，一个十几岁的男孩。男人走在最前面，手里攥着一根从什么地方拆下来的铁管，女人紧紧拉着男孩的手，男孩背上背着一个鼓鼓囊囊的书包，跑几步就回头看一眼，像是怕有什么东西从后面追上来。

“正门注意，三点钟方向，三人，两个成人一个小孩，距离大概两百米，正在靠近。”大刘的声音从对讲机里传出来，平稳而清晰。

林越正蹲在配电房后面的荒地上和赵德柱一起翻土，听到对讲机的声音，站起来拍了拍手上的泥。“赵叔，你继续。我去门口。”

赵德柱头也没抬，短柄锄头一下一下地刨进土里。“去吧。这块地今天得翻完。”

林越走到正门的时候，赵铭已经在铁门后面等着了。他把工兵铲杵在身前，站姿笔直，脸上的表情是那种安保人员特有的职业性严肃。老郑站在他旁边，手里握着一把户外刀，刀刃朝下贴在腿侧，姿态很松弛，但眼睛一眨不眨地盯着铁门上的观察孔。

“开门还是不开？”赵铭问。

“先看。”林越凑到观察孔前。

三个人已经到了铁丝网外围。男人大概四十出头，穿着一件沾满灰尘的灰色夹克，脸上有一道还在渗血的抓痕——不是咬伤，是指甲抓的，可能是混乱中被其他人挠到的。女人大概三十多岁，头发散乱，左脚的鞋跑丢了一只，光着的脚板上全是泥和细小的石子印。男孩站在他们身后，书包带子在胸前打了两个死结，脸上脏得看不出本来的肤色，但眼睛里没有哭过的红肿——在这种逃难路上没哭过的孩子，要么吓傻了，要么比大人想象的要坚强得多。

男人看到了围墙上的哨塔，也看到了铁丝网上的毛刺在阳光下闪光。他没有继续往前走，而是停在铁丝网外面大概五米的地方，把铁管放在地上，双手举过头顶。

“我们不咬人！”他的声音沙哑得像是用砂纸刮过喉咙，“我们没被咬——真的，我们自己检查过了。能不能让我们进去？孩子一晚上没吃东西了。”

林越看了一眼老郑。老郑从观察孔里仔细打量了那个男人的瞳孔和裸露的皮肤，然后微微点了一下头。“瞳孔没散，皮肤颜色正常，没有抽搐。抓痕是旧的，已经结痂了。目测没有感染迹象。”

“开门。”林越说。

赵铭把铁门拉开一道仅容一人通过的缝隙。老郑闪身出去，刀刃仍然贴在腿侧，走到三个人面前。他先把地上的铁管捡起来放到一边，然后让三个人站成一排，从头到脚目视检查了一遍——脖子、手臂、小腿，所有裸露的皮肤。然后又让他们转过身，检查后背。

男孩看了男人一眼，男人点了一下头。男孩把书包解下来，拉开拉链。里面是两瓶矿泉水、半包饼干、一个作业本和一个铅笔盒。老郑看了一眼，把书包还给他。

“进来。进门之后先登记。你们会被隔离观察六个小时。这是规矩。”

男人的喉结上下滚动了一下，声音比刚才更哑了。“谢谢。谢谢你们。”

三个人被带进正门旁边临时划出来的隔离区——那是冷库管理间最外面的一间房，里面放了一张折叠桌、几把椅子和一箱矿泉水。阿青已经背着急救包等在门口了。他让三个人坐下，先用体温枪挨个测了体温，然后

“你是医生？”女人看着阿青熟练的动作，声音里终于有了一丝活气。

“卫生员。”阿青说，手里的棉签稳稳地在伤口边缘画着圈，“当过兵，会处理外伤。你们从哪里过来的？”

“城南。”男人的声音很低，像是怕被什么东西听到，“昨天下午机场出事的时候我们正好在北边串亲戚。要是当时在家，现在——”他没有说完。

林越站在隔离间门口，隔着门框看着这一家人。男孩正在用袖子擦脸上的灰，擦了两下露出下面白净的皮肤，然后从书包里掏出那半包饼干，先递给他妈妈，又递给他爸爸。男人没有接，女人也没有。他们把饼干推回男孩手里。

“林哥。”赵铭走到他身后，压低声音，“刚才那个男人说他们是从城南过来的，但出事的时候在北边。运气不错。”

“不是运气。”林越说，“昨天是周一，他们一家人去北边串亲戚——说明他们周一不上班不上学。可能是请假了，也可能是自由职业。不管哪种，他们比大部分城南居民多活了一天。”

赵铭沉默了片刻。“后面还会有更多吗？”

“会。”林越转过身，看着正门外那条土路。阳光已经把路面晒得发白，远处的国道上隐约可以看到几个黑点在移动，是人还是丧尸，距离太远看不清。“今天是末世第二天，能自己走到这里的都是第一波幸运的人。再过两天，能走到这里的就不一定是幸运的人了。”

他没有展开解释这句话。但赵铭听懂了——两天之后，能活着穿过半个城区摸到北郊的人，要么是真的运气爆表，要么是足够危险才能活下来。末世第二年之后，幸存者里最可怕的东西不是丧尸病毒，是人心。

上午十点，第二拨幸存者到了。这次只有一个人。

一个穿深蓝色工装的男人，三十岁上下，骑着自行车，车后座绑着一个工具包。他在国道路口停了一下，看到物流园的围墙和铁丝网，犹豫了大概三十秒，然后重新蹬上车，朝正门骑过来。

老郑在门口拦住了他。和之前一样的检查流程——瞳孔、皮肤、裸露部位，全部无异常。工具包里装的是一套电工工具和两个万用表。

“你是电工？”老郑问。

“电力公司的。城北变电站的。”男人的声音很急促，但条理清楚，“昨天下午变电站自动保护跳闸了，我跟三个同事留守值班，半夜的时候外面全是枪声和尖叫声。早上枪声停了，我们分开跑。我往这边来的。你们这里有电吗？”

老郑没有回答这个问题。他把男人带进隔离间，和阿青一起做了检查，然后通过对讲机叫来了王浩。

王浩从配电房跑过来，看到工具包里的万用表和绝缘胶带，眼睛亮了一下，但脸上的表情还是板着的——他在陌生人面前总是下意识地先板着脸。

“你说你是变电站的？多少千伏的站？”

“一百一。”男人说，“我是二次设备检修组的。”

“继电保护？”

At nine o'clock in the morning, the first group of survivors appeared at the national road intersection.

When Da Liu saw them from the east sentry tower, the three men were bending and trotting along the drainage ditch on the north side of the national highway.A man, a woman, a teenage boy.The man walked in the front, holding an iron pipe removed from somewhere in his hand. The woman held the boy's hand tightly. The boy carried a bulging schoolbag on his back. After running a few steps, he looked back, as if he was afraid that something would catch up from behind.

"Attention at the main entrance, three o'clock direction, three people, two adults and one child, about two hundred meters away, approaching." Da Liu's voice came from the intercom, steady and clear.

Lin Yue was squatting on the wasteland behind the power distribution room and digging soil with Zhao Dezhu. When he heard the sound of the intercom, he stood up and patted the mud on his hands."Uncle Zhao, you continue. I'll go to the door."

Zhao Dezhu didn't even raise his head, and dug the short-handled hoe into the soil one by one."Go ahead. This land needs to be plowed today."

When Lin Yue walked to the main entrance, Zhao Ming was already waiting behind the iron gate.He shoveled the engineer in front of him, stood upright, and the expression on his face was the professional seriousness unique to security personnel.Lao Zheng stood next to him, holding an outdoor knife in his hand, with the blade facing down against the side of his leg. His posture was very relaxed, but his eyes were staring at the observation hole on the iron door without blinking.

"Open the door or not?" Zhao Ming asked.

"Look first." Lin Yue approached the observation hole.

The three people have reached the outside of the barbed wire fence.The man was probably in his early forties, wearing a dusty gray jacket. There was a scratch on his face that was still bleeding—not a bite, but a fingernail scratch, maybe scratched by someone else in the chaos.The woman was probably in her thirties, with disheveled hair. She had lost one of her left shoes, and her bare feet were covered with mud and tiny pebble marks.The boy stood behind them, with his schoolbag strap tied in two tight knots on his chest. His face was so dirty that the original color of his skin could not be seen, but his eyes were not red or swollen from crying. Children who had never cried during this kind of escape were either scared out of their wits, or they were much stronger than adults imagined.

The man saw the sentry tower on the wall and the burrs on the barbed wire flashing in the sun.He did not continue walking forward, but stopped about five meters outside the barbed wire fence, placed the iron pipe on the ground, and raised his hands above his head.

"We don't bite!" His voice was hoarse as if sandpaper had been scraped across his throat. "We haven't been bitten - really, we checked ourselves. Can you let us in? The child hasn't eaten anything all night."

Lin Yue glanced at Lao Zheng.Lao Zheng carefully looked at the man's pupils and exposed skin through the observation hole, and then nodded slightly."The pupils are not dilated, the skin color is normal, and there is no twitching. The scratches are old and have scabbed over. There is no visual sign of infection."

"Open the door." Lin Yue said.

Zhao Ming opened the iron door to a gap that allowed only one person to pass through.Lao Zheng stepped out, the blade still attached to the side of his leg, and walked in front of the three people.He first picked up the iron pipes on the ground and put them aside, then asked three people to stand in a row and visually inspected them from head to toe - neck, arms, calves, all exposed skin.Then they were asked to turn around and check their backs.

The boy glanced at the man, and the man nodded.The boy took off his schoolbag and unzipped it.Inside were two bottles of mineral water, half a pack of biscuits, an exercise book and a pencil case.Lao Zheng took a look and returned his schoolbag to him.

"Come in. Register first after entering. You will be quarantined and observed for six hours. This is the rule."

The man's Adam's apple rolled up and down, and his voice became hoarse than before."Thank you. Thank you."

The three people were taken into a temporary isolation area next to the main entrance - it was the outermost room of the cold storage management room. There was a folding table, a few chairs and a box of mineral water in it.Ah Qing was already waiting at the door with a first aid kit on his back.He asked the three people to sit down, first took their temperatures one by one with a thermometer gun, and then

"Are you a doctor?" The woman looked at Ah Qing's skillful movements, and finally there was a hint of vitality in her voice.

"Hygienist," Ah Qing said, drawing a steady circle on the edge of the wound with the cotton swab in his hand. "I was a soldier and know how to deal with trauma. Where did you come from?"

"South of the city." The man's voice was very low, as if he was afraid of being heard. "Yesterday afternoon when something happened at the airport, we happened to be visiting relatives in the north. If we were at home at that time, now-" He did not finish.

Lin Yue stood at the door of the isolation room, looking at the family through the door frame.The boy was wiping the ashes on his face with his sleeve, wiping twice to reveal the fair skin underneath. Then he took out the half pack of biscuits from his schoolbag and handed it first to his mother and then to his father.The man didn't answer, and neither did the woman.They pushed the cookies back into the boy's hands.

"Brother Lin." Zhao Ming walked behind him and lowered his voice, "The man just now said that they came from the south of the city, but they were in the north when the accident happened. They were lucky."

"It's not luck." Lin Yue said, "Yesterday was Monday, and their family went to visit relatives in the north - which means they don't go to work or go to school on Monday. Maybe they asked for leave, or maybe they are freelance. No matter which way, they lived one day longer than most residents in the south of the city."

Zhao Ming was silent for a moment."Will there be more to come?"

"Yes." Lin Yue turned around and looked at the dirt road outside the main entrance.The sun has turned the road white, and a few black spots can be vaguely seen moving on the national highway in the distance. Whether they are people or zombies, it is too far to see clearly."Today is the second day of the apocalypse. Those who can get here by themselves are the first wave of lucky people. In two days, those who can get here are not necessarily the lucky ones."

He did not elaborate on this statement.But Zhao Ming understood - after two days, those who can survive through half of the city and reach the northern suburbs must either be really lucky or be in enough danger to survive.After the second year of the apocalypse, the most terrifying thing among survivors is not the zombie virus, but the human heart.

At ten o'clock in the morning, the second group of survivors arrived.This time there was only one person.

A man in dark blue overalls, about thirty years old, was riding a bicycle with a tool bag strapped to the back seat of the bicycle.He stopped at the intersection of the national road and saw the wall and barbed wire fence of the logistics park. He hesitated for about thirty seconds, then got on the car again and rode towards the main entrance.

Lao Zheng stopped him at the door.The same inspection process as before - pupils, skin, exposed parts, all normal.The tool bag contained a set of electrical tools and two multimeters.

"Are you an electrician?" Lao Zheng asked.

"From the electric power company. From the substation in the north of the city." The man's voice was urgent but clear. "The automatic protection of the substation tripped yesterday afternoon. Three colleagues and I stayed on duty. In the middle of the night, there were gunshots and screams outside. In the morning, the gunfire stopped and we ran separately. I came this way. Do you have electricity here?"

Lao Zheng did not answer this question.He took the man into the isolation room, did an examination with Ah Qing, and then called Wang Hao through the intercom.

Wang Hao ran over from the power distribution room and saw the multimeter and insulating tape in the tool bag. His eyes lit up, but the expression on his face was still serious - he always subconsciously kept a straight face in front of strangers.

"You said you work at a substation? How many kilovolts is it?"

"One hundred and one." The man said, "I'm from the secondary equipment maintenance team."

"Relay protection?"
